A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mimic Score and Grad-Mimic research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v4 reports original noisy-label image-classification experiments, CLIP training and filtering results, and appendix experiments on efficiency, aggregation, reference-model robustness, and membership prediction.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds Pythia-160M experiments on four text question-answering datasets, reporting negative log-likelihood results in Table 15.

M1.justification: The gradient-projection Mimic Score, softmax batch reweighting, score binarization, and weak-supervision aggregation remain unchanged in Equations 1–3 and Algorithms 1–2. The Pythia experiment applies the existing procedure without introducing a documented method component.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds text-only science question answering on ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, SciQ, and OpenBookQA. This substantially extends the evaluated domain beyond v4’s image classification and image-text training, while retaining all previous coverage.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their comparator membership. The added text experiment extends the existing comparison against uniform training and approximate influence functions. The new FLOP table likewise uses baseline methods already included in Figure 8.

E3.justification: The added text experiment adapts the existing noisy-label protocol to Pythia-160M, with 20% and 30% random-distractor answer corruption, a clean validation set sized at 10% of training data for reference construction, and checkpoint NLL evaluation. Previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds an analytical breakdown of per-batch FLOP costs and their dependence on parameter counts, batch size, and validation-set size. This supplements the existing runtime and memory analysis. Existing temperature, layer-choice, reference-quality, aggregation, and data-utilization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The five independent aggregation-subset trials and reference-seed variance reporting are unchanged, including v4 Table 15 becoming v5 Table 17. The added text results introduce no run-count disclosure, uncertainty intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 15 adds a new language-model result suite across four tasks and two noise levels, with Grad-Mimic reporting the lowest NLL in all eight settings. For SciQ at 20% noise, its NLL is 1.456 versus 1.528 for SFT and 1.621 for influence functions. Matched pre-existing results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The convergence assumptions, lemmas, theorem, and proofs are retained, with Appendix 9 becoming Appendix A. Appendix E newly derives a simplified FLOP model, assuming backward cost B approximately equals 2F and obtaining Grad-Mimic’s additional per-batch cost of (2n + 2)d_L, alongside comparator cost expressions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about Mimic Score, two-stage selection, efficiency, and filtering effectiveness. The headline 20.7% training-step reduction and 4.7-million-sample reduction are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly interprets the Pythia results as evidence of modality-independent scoring. Appendix I extends the existing reference-dependency discussion using the text experiment’s small reference-training set. The requirement for matching reference and trained-model architectures remains explicit.

D1.justification: v4 only promises future source-code release; v5 adds a release statement and GitHub link in the abstract, although Appendix C retains the future-release wording. The new text experiment also documents its model, answer-corruption procedure, and reference-set size.

R1.justification: v5 adds references for Pythia, ARC, SciQ, and OpenBookQA to support the text experiments. The main related-work positioning remains stable. Changes to authors, venues, and other metadata for retained references do not introduce different comparison methods or cited works.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, clarifies reference-model sourcing and scoring explanations, and changes appendix labels from 9–17 to A–I. Future Work becomes Discussion and Future Work, with an added reference-dependency discussion; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v5 adds the FLOP comparison and text-task NLL tables as Tables 7 and 15. Existing tables are renumbered and repositioned as the appendices reflow. All ten figures retain their visual content, and the basic page design remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 15 supplies direct text-only evidence for the method’s broader applicability, while Appendix E makes its efficiency reasoning more explicit. The code link also improves access information. These are useful but limited gains: the text study covers one 160M model and reports no uncertainty or convergence curves despite claiming faster convergence, and the code-release statements remain inconsistent. The revision strengthens supporting evidence without resolving a major methodological deficiency.
